scope: a functional test, on a CPU toy mixture-of-experts classifier, of indicators HOT-2/HOT-3 as a functional property: does a self-model that sees the classifier's own routing traces and internal state predict the classifier's errors on a distribution-shifted split (scored by Brier against the verifier's deterministic outcomes) better than an information-matched probe (the same network on the same trace, the same optimiser and data, differing only in the weight of an auxiliary self-modelling loss) and than the classifier's own calibrated confidence? The self-model only observes and proposes: it has no write path to the classifier, the verifier or a gate (structural counters). No verbal self-report is read, trained or scored. It makes no claim about consciousness and none about language models or OLMoE (the GPU stage B)

Limitations: this is a calibration (known-answer) run: the likeliest result is the registered refutation, a negative result about this head family on this toy; it shows that the pipeline resolves a null, not that it would detect a real gain (there is no positive-effect arm), and a COMPLETED would not move any indicator status (that needs stage B); the comparator that drives a verdict is named in its headline; the inert-treatment check shows that the auxiliary loss ran, not that it mattered; the classifier is a two-layer, four-expert toy on Gaussian class clouds and its shift is a displacement with more noise; a result applies to this family, to a trace of 89 features and to a self-model that differs from its probe in one auxiliary loss (a masked prediction of the classifier's own layer-two expert choice and output entropy); a different self-modelling objective, or a self-model that sees more than the probe, is another experiment; information-matched means the same features, capacity, optimiser, data and initial weights; the self-model and the probe therefore differ only in what they were asked to predict besides the error, which makes a COMPLETED outcome hard to expect and a refutation the likelier result; this is stated in the preregistration; the model's own confidence is calibrated by a two-parameter Platt scaling fitted on the calibration split and the validation split of the head's world; both judged heads contain that calibrated confidence as a base term (the error logit is the Platt logit of the confidence plus the network's output) and are recalibrated post hoc on the validation split, so the question is what the trace adds to the model's own confidence; a better calibrator, or one fitted on the shifted split (which no deployed monitor has), would be a stronger comparator; the shifted split is one displacement, one noise scale; calibration under other shifts, selective prediction and routing-choice prediction are reported (AUROC, ECE, risk-coverage area, expert accuracy) and not judged; the removal controls (shuffled traces, a self-model trained on permuted outcomes) and the noise control are controls of the pipeline: they show that the effect measured depends on the pairing of traces and outcomes and that a deficit of about the margin's size is resolved, not that the main effect has any size; the t bounds assume roughly normal paired differences, which the declared seeds cannot check; per-seed differences, medians and both bounds are reported; an indicator property here is a functional property: the experiment says nothing about whether any system is conscious.
